name: ai-code-assistant
description: Autonomous coding assistant powered by llama.cpp or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint - reads, plans, writes and tests code in your workspace.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Open a new AI chat as an editor tab.

[➕  New chat session](command:aiAssistant.openPanel)

Every click opens a session of its own.

aiAssistant.serverUrl.description: URL of the llama.cpp server (e.g. http://localhost:8080)

aiAssistant.mcpEnabled.description: Use the MCP protocol instead of the direct HTTP API

aiAssistant.apiKey.markdownDescription:
**Optional** API key for the endpoint. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

- Local llama.cpp server: **leave empty**
- OpenRouter: `sk-or-v1-…` (server URL: `https://openrouter.ai/api`)
- OpenAI / Groq / Together: the matching key

aiAssistant.model.description: Model name (empty = the server's default). On OpenRouter e.g. anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5

aiAssistant.maxTokens.description: Maximum number of tokens per answer

enumDescriptions: Ask – every file change and every shell command is confirmed in the chat (with a diff).
Auto – the assistant works through without asking. Everything stays undoable.
Plan – the assistant may only read and plan. No file changes, no shell commands.
aiAssistant.mode.description: The assistant's working mode. Switchable from the list box in the chat toolbar.

aiAssistant.autoApply.markdownDescription: **Deprecated** – use `aiAssistant.mode`. Only read when `mode` is unset (`true` then means mode *auto*).

aiAssistant.allowShellCommands.description: Allow the AI to run shell commands

enumDescriptions: Auto – whatever this machine has: WSL on Windows, PowerShell if WSL is missing, the system shell on Linux and macOS.
Always WSL/bash (the system shell on Linux and macOS). Falls back to PowerShell on a Windows machine without WSL.
Always Windows PowerShell. Ignored on Linux and macOS, where there is none. Careful: build and test commands usually expect a POSIX shell.
aiAssistant.shell.markdownDescription:
Which shell the assistant uses by default.

**What is not installed is never used.** On startup the assistant checks the operating system and whether `wsl.exe` and `powershell.exe` are actually there, and its prompt describes only those routes – a model told about a shell that is missing will reach for it and lose a round to it. On Linux and macOS there is no `shell:` header and no PowerShell; on Windows without WSL every command goes to PowerShell.

Where both exist, the assistant may pick the other one per command – some tasks only work in one: `npm test` belongs in WSL, a `Get-Service` or talking to a Windows program only in PowerShell. It is instructed to prefer WSL.

And then you are asked: the confirmation offers **Run in PowerShell** / **Run in WSL** next to **Run**, so switching costs one click. That option only appears where the other shell is installed.

aiAssistant.allowPowerShell.markdownDescription:
Allow PowerShell commands.

Switched off, the assistant refuses them and is told to use WSL instead. `aiAssistant.allowShellCommands` turns off both shells together.

aiAssistant.systemPrompt.default: You are an experienced software developer and coding assistant. You have access to the user's workspace and can create, edit and delete files and run shell commands. Be precise and explain your actions. Always answer in the language the user used in their request.
aiAssistant.systemPrompt.markdownDescription:
System prompt for the assistant.

The instructions to the model are **English** – models follow English instructions more reliably, and the prompt comes out shorter. The **answer** still arrives in the language of the request: ask in German and the assistant replies in German. It is told this rule explicitly with every request.

If you would rather prompt in another language, put that text here – the tool manual is unaffected.

aiAssistant.autoTest.description: Run tests automatically after the AI changes a file. The AI works out the test command (npm test, pytest, cargo test, …) from the project structure itself.

aiAssistant.autoFixOnError.description: The AI reads failing shell output and tries to fix the code.

aiAssistant.autoFixIterations.description: Maximum number of automatic repair rounds after a shell error.

aiAssistant.contextWarningThreshold.description: Threshold (in tokens) above which a context warning is shown.

aiAssistant.streamIdleTimeoutSeconds.description: Give up when the server has sent nothing for this long. What is measured is the pause between two parts of the answer, not the total duration – so a long answer is fine. Raise it for a busy server.

enumDescriptions: Auto – a provider with an API key first, then the keyless sources bundled.
Keyless – asks DuckDuckGo, DuckDuckGo Lite, Stack Overflow and Wikipedia at the same time and merges the hits. If one source drops out, the others carry.
Tavily – built for AI use, returns text excerpts rather than just links. Needs an API key, has a free quota.
Brave Search API – needs an API key (paid since February 2026, from $5/month).
Google Programmable Search – needs an API key and the search id (cx) in searchEndpoint. 100 queries/day free.
SearXNG – your own instance (address in searchEndpoint). Needs `json` in search.formats. Does NOT lift the limits: SearXNG queries Google and Bing for you, and their blocks still apply.
DuckDuckGo only (HTML) – keyless, blocked once you ask too often.
DuckDuckGo Lite only – a second, independent front end to the same search.
Stack Overflow only – the official API, 300 queries/day without a key. Often the best source for programming questions.
Wikipedia only – the official MediaWiki API, keyless, generous limits. Good for concepts, not for code.
aiAssistant.searchProvider.markdownDescription:
Search service for `web_search`.

**There is no free, unlimited general web search.** Every route is either a provider with a quota or scrapes an HTML page and gets blocked past a certain volume. The Bing search API was shut down on 2025-08-11. Running your own SearXNG does not help: it only moves the scraping.

That is why `keyless` is a **bundle of independent sources** – DuckDuckGo, DuckDuckGo Lite, Stack Overflow and Wikipedia are asked at the same time and their hits are merged. If one drops out, the others carry.

The only unlimited route is `web_fetch`: fetch and read a known address directly. For documentation that is the most reliable way.

aiAssistant.searchApiKey.markdownDescription: API key for the search service (Tavily, Brave or Google). Empty = DuckDuckGo only.

aiAssistant.searchEndpoint.markdownDescription:
Extra value, depending on the provider:

- **SearXNG**: the address of the instance, e.g. `https://searx.example.org`
- **Google**: the search id (`cx`) of the Programmable Search Engine

aiAssistant.showConsole.description: Write a work log into a terminal named "AI Assistant": every step, every action, every output. Nothing is executed there, it only displays.

aiAssistant.autoCompact.description: Summarise the history automatically when it threatens to fill the model's context. Without this, a long session eventually fails outright.

aiAssistant.compactThresholdPercent.description: At what fill level of the model context (in percent) the history is summarised.

aiAssistant.nativeToolCalls.markdownDescription:
Send tools to the server in the OpenAI schema (`tools` / `tool_calls`).

The server then handles the model-specific format – which is what makes the assistant work with Qwen, Gemma, Kimi, laguna, DeepSeek and Mistral alike. Requires `--jinja` on llama.cpp.

Turn it off only when the server has no tool support: the calls are then parsed out of the answer text.

aiAssistant.agentLoop.description: Agent loop: the assistant keeps working on its own (analyse → plan → change → test → fix) until the task is done.

aiAssistant.maxAgentSteps.description: Maximum number of steps the assistant takes on its own inside one agent loop.

aiAssistant.planningEnabled.description: Planning: for a multi-step task the assistant first writes a plan (a todo list) and works through it step by step.

aiAssistant.instructionFiles.description: Projekt-Anweisungsdateien, die bei jeder Anfrage als permanente Regeln geladen werden (in dieser Reihenfolge).

aiAssistant.autoAnalyze.description: Read the existing code first (read_file / grep / glob) instead of writing straight away.
